0.headline: BLS Polymers GMP at 44% ahead of listing tomorrow; should investors buy, sell or hold? Here's what analysts say
0.heading: BLS Polymers GMP at 44% ahead of listing tomorrow; should investors buy, sell or hold? Here's what analysts say
0.intro: BLS Polymers shares are commanding a strong premium in the grey market ahead of their stock market debut on November 3, with the company's initial public offering (IPO) attracting overwhelming investor interest during the subscription period.
0.body:
BLS Polymers shares are commanding a strong premium in the grey market ahead of their stock market debut on November 3, with the company's initial public offering (IPO) attracting overwhelming investor interest during the subscription period.

The Rs 255-crore IPO is currently commanding a grey market premium (GMP) of Rs 66 per share, or around 44 percent, as of November 2, according to InvestorGain. At the upper end of the IPO price band of Rs 150, the GMP indicates a potential listing price of Rs 216 per share.

However, the grey market premium is an unofficial indicator of investor sentiment and does not guarantee listing gains. It can fluctuate depending on market conditions and demand ahead of the listing.

Read Also: From table cleaner to Rs 1,700-crore food business: How K S Thirupathi Raja built Adyar Ananda Bhavan (A2B)

The strong grey market premium comes after the IPO received an impressive response from investors, with the issue subscribed 241.22 times, according to NSE data. Investors placed bids for 287.05 crore shares against 1.19 crore shares on offer.

The non-institutional investor (NII) category led the demand, with its reserved portion subscribed 559.20 times. The qualified institutional buyer (QIB) category was subscribed 200.25 times, while the retail investor portion received bids for 128.36 times the shares reserved for it.

The IPO opened for subscription on October 27 and closed on October 29. The company had fixed the price band at Rs 142-150 per share, valuing it at approximately Rs 930.5 crore at the upper end of the price band.

The issue comprised an entirely fresh issue of 1.7 crore equity shares. The company will use the proceeds to fund its expansion and working capital requirements.

Of the total proceeds, Rs 77.56 crore has been earmarked for expanding its existing manufacturing facility in Goa, while Rs 89.5 crore will be utilised towards working capital requirements. The remaining amount will be used for general corporate purposes.

The allotment was scheduled to be finalised on October 30, while refunds and credit of shares to demat accounts were expected on November 2. BLS Polymers shares are scheduled to list on the BSE and NSE on November 3.

Should you buy, sell or hold?

Commenting on the company's listing prospects and investment outlook, Narendra Solanki, Head of Fundamental Research – Investment Services at Anand Rathi Shares and Stock Brokers, said BLS Polymers is positioned to benefit from rising investments in infrastructure sectors.

"BLS Polymers is well-positioned to benefit from rising investments in power, telecom, railway and pipeline infrastructure, supported by its diversified product portfolio, customised manufacturing capabilities and established market presence," Solanki said.

Check IPO News Here

On the listing outlook, Solanki expects the stock to make a decent debut.

"The company is expected to list at a decent premium. Investors may continue to hold the stock from a long-term perspective or partially book profits," he said.

About BLS Polymers

Based in New Delhi, BLS Polymers manufactures custom-formulated polymer compounds in different grades for industrial applications.

Its products are used as raw materials for the sheathing, jacketing and insulation of wires and cables deployed across the power, telecommunications and railway sectors. The company's polymer compounds are also used to coat underground oil, gas and water pipelines, helping protect them against corrosion and external environmental factors.

BLS Polymers currently operates a manufacturing facility in Goa equipped with 11 dedicated production machines. The proposed expansion is aimed at increasing the production capacity of selected products.

1.headline: Wall Street brokers rush in with bullish calls on NSE
1.heading: Wall Street brokers rush in with bullish calls on NSE
1.intro: Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan Chase & Co. have initiated coverage of NSE’s stock with overweight ratings, even as it has mostly traded below its IPO price since listing in September
1.body:
The National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. is winning bullish backing from Wall Street brokers, as they expect the bourse’s dominance to gain in India’s deepening capital markets.

Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan Chase & Co. have initiated coverage of NSE’s stock with overweight ratings, even as it has mostly traded below its initial public offering price since listing in September. India’s 360 ONE Capital Markets Pvt. also recommends buying the stock.

The optimism reflects confidence in the structural expansion of India’s capital markets despite near-term concerns over slowing derivatives growth. A widening investor base in the world’s most populous nation and rising trading activity could benefit its top exchange regardless of market direction.

Morgan Stanley is the most bullish with a 2,315-rupee price target for 12 months, implying an upside of as much as 30% from Friday’s closing price. JPMorgan sees the shares reaching 2,130 rupees, while 360 ONE has a 2,100-rupee target. Affiliates of the three firms were among the banks that worked on NSE’s IPO.

Jefferies also has a buy recommendation on NSE, while Macquarie Capital rated it outperform.

NSE is an “engine of India’s capital markets,” Morgan Stanley said, terming the exchange a strong play on financialization of household savings and a shift toward equities. India’s markets remain underpenetrated, with just 3.2% of working-age Indians trading in NSE’s cash market and 0.7% trading equity derivatives, it said.

The brokerage expects NSE’s dominant position and asset-light business model to support premium valuations. NSE has more than 90% share in the cash-equities market and nearly all of equity futures and single-stock options, while its index-options share appears to have stabilized at about 65%, it said.

New businesses, including commodities, a mutual-fund ordering platform and electronic gold receipts, could reduce NSE’s reliance on equity options and add about 15% to revenue and profit by fiscal 2030, according to Jefferies.

“A recovery in capital market conditions, coupled with the potential upside from smaller revenue streams, could further aid earnings,” Swarnabha Mukherjee, an analyst at 360 ONE, wrote in a note.

2.headline: Bombay Coated & Special Steels IPO subscribed 7x so far on Day 3; check latest GMP
2.heading: Bombay Coated & Special Steels IPO subscribed 7x so far on Day 3; check latest GMP
2.intro: The initial public offering (IPO) of Bombay Coated & Special Steels continued to witness strong investor interest on the last day of bidding, with the issue receiving 7 times subscription by 10:40 am on October 30, as per NSE data.
2.body:
The initial public offering (IPO) of Bombay Coated &amp; Special Steels continued to witness strong investor interest on the last day of bidding, with the issue receiving 7 times subscription by 10:40 am on October 30, as per NSE data.

The Rs 183.06 crore IPO received bids for 11,57,74,386 shares against 1,65,33,012 shares on offer. Non-institutional investors led the demand with 9.40 times subscription, followed by qualified institutional buyers with 6.57 times subscription.

In the grey market, Bombay Coated &amp; Special Steels shares were commanding a premium of 11 percent on the morning of November 2, according to InvestorGain. However, the GMP is an unofficial indicator of investor sentiment and does not guarantee the listing price or returns.

Read Also: M K Sons Fine Jewels IPO allotment today; check status on BSE, NSE and registrar

The company has fixed the price band for the issue at Rs 78-82 per share. Investors can apply for a minimum of 182 shares in one lot, requiring an investment of Rs 14,924 at the upper end of the price band.

The tentative listing date for Bombay Coated &amp; Special Steels shares on the BSE and NSE is November 5.

The IPO comprises an entirely fresh issue of shares worth Rs 183.06 crore. The company plans to utilise a substantial portion of the proceeds to reduce its debt and meet costs associated with capital equipment.

Of the net proceeds, Rs 125 crore will be used to repay or prepay certain borrowings. Another Rs 15.77 crore has been earmarked for costs related to acquiring capital equipment under existing lease arrangements with Siemens Financial Services Pvt. Ltd. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

Check IPO News Here

Bombay Coated &amp; Special Steels reported an improvement in its revenue and profit in fiscal 2026. Revenue from operations rose to Rs 1,266.82 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,055.71 crore in FY25. The company had reported revenue of Rs 755.26 crore in FY24.

Profit after tax (PAT) increased to Rs 30.54 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 28.67 crore in FY25 and Rs 21.14 crore in FY24.

For the quarter ended June 2026, the company reported revenue from operations of Rs 397.08 crore and a profit after tax of Rs 15.08 crore.

About Bombay Coated &amp; Special Steels

Bombay Coated &amp; Special Steels is a steel processing company that converts steel coils into processed steel products through operations such as slitting, cut-to-length processing, shearing and embossing.

The company's manufacturing facilities are located in Wada and Bhiwandi in Maharashtra, Ghiloth in Rajasthan, and Sri City in Andhra Pradesh.

It caters to industrial customers that require processed steel for their operations. As of June 30, 2026, the company had an aggregate installed processing capacity of 1,23,153 tonnes per annum.
